correctness.rationale: The fixed-translation orthonormal bases give full frame operator pI; subtracting the deleted synthesis product yields the sharp lower bound p minus the largest erased Gram eigenvalue. Rank at most three leaves the surviving upper eigenvalue exactly p. Distinct translation slopes have overlap magnitude p^(-1/2) by the quadratic Gauss sum; the one-class and two-class cases give erased top eigenvalues 1 and 1+sqrt(2/p). For three classes, complete the square on each directed edge and cancel the constant phases cyclically. The quadratic identity for the cyclic squares can be checked after subtracting from beta the affine function matching the first two values (the sum is invariant and R is unchanged). The resulting normalized product is epsilon_p^3 chi(P) omega^(R²/(4P)); the cycle contributes 2 cos(theta) to the scaled off-diagonal cubic, whose largest root is 2 cos(|theta|/3). In the 1 mod 4 case square P and R=0 attain phase zero. In the 3 mod 4 case the angular units of pi/(2p) are odd; with chi(P)=1 and R²=P, 4^(-1)=(p+1)/4 gives exactly pi/(2p). For slopes 0,1,u the number of u giving a nonzero square P=u(1-u) is (p−2−chi(−1))/2>0, and varying beta realizes every R. Both attained eigenvalues strictly exceed 1+sqrt(2/p), and converting the surviving frame eigenvalue ratio to singular values gives the stated square-root condition number.
residual_risks: The numerical replay is bounded and uses floating-point tolerance. Arbitrary primes, exact attainment and positivity of the surviving lower frame bound follow from the proof, not numerics.
